title: Standard Time Interpretation Of References Ordinance 1943

sections.shortTitle: Standard Time Interpretation Of References Ordinance 1943
sections.description:
Short title and commencement

THE STANDARD TIME (INTERPRETATION OF REFERENCES) ORDINANCE, 1943
THE STANDARD TIME
(INTERPRETATION OF REFERENCES) ORDINANCE, 1943.
ORDINANCE No. VI of 1943
(The Ordinance has been applied to‑
(i) the partially excluded areas of the Mymensingh District,
with effect from the 8th April, 1943, see Ben. Govt. Notification No. 1412‑P.,
dated the 27th March, 1943;
(ii) Baluchistan, see Notification No. 18‑W., dated the
8th February, 1943, Gazette of India, 1943, Pt. I, p. 192;
(iii) such of the Baluoh tribal areas beyond the western
border of the Dera Ghazi Khan District of the Punjab as are not included in the
Baluchistan tribal areas, in so far as the same may be applicable and subject
to any amendments to which it is for the time being subject in the Provinces,
etc., see Notification No. 27‑W., dated the 3rd March, 1943, Gazette of
India, 1943, Pt. I, p. 266.
It has been extended to the Leased Areas of Baluchistan by
the Leased Areas (Laws) Order, 1950 (G. G. O. 3 of 1950).
This Ordinance has been extended to the whole of Pakistan
with effect from the 14th October, 1955, by the Central Laws (Statute Reform)
Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch.
)
[20th January,
1943]
An Ordinance to provide for the interpretation in
enactments in force in (See footnote 2 on page 450,
infra.)[Pakistan] of references to (The word
"Indian" rep. by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declara tion) Act,
1951 (26 of 1951), s. 3 and 2nd Sch.)* Standard Time.
WHEREAS an emergency has arisen
which makes it necessary to provide for the interpretation in enactments in
force in (See footnote 2 on page 450, infra.)[Pakistan]
of references to (The word "Indian" rep. by
the Federal Laws (Revision and Declara tion) Act, 1951 (26 of 1951), s. 3 and
2nd Sch.)* Standard Time ;
Now, THEREFORE, in exercise of
the powers conferred by section 72 of the Government of India Act, as set out
in the Ninth Schedule to the Government of India Act, 1935, the Governor‑General
is pleased to make and promulgate the following Ordinance :‑ 26 Geo
5,c,2.
1. Short title and
commencement-----‑(1) This Ordinance may be called the (The word "Indian" rep. by the Federal Laws
(Revision and Declara tion) Act, 1951 (26 of 1951), s. 3 and 2nd Sch.)*
Standard Time (Interpretation of References) Ordinance, 1943.
(2) It shall come into force at
once.

sections.shortTitle: Standard Time Interpretation Of References Ordinance 1943
sections.description:
Interpretation of references to standard Time

THE STANDARD TIME (INTERPRETATION OF REFERENCES) ORDINANCE, 1943
THE STANDARD TIME
(INTERPRETATION OF REFERENCES) ORDINANCE, 1943.
ORDINANCE No. VI of 1943
[20th January,
1943]
An Ordinance to provide for the interpretation in
enactments in force in (See footnote 2 on page 450,
infra.)[Pakistan] of references to (The word
"Indian" rep. by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declara tion) Act,
1951 (26 of 1951), s. 3 and 2nd Sch.)* Standard Time.
WHEREAS an emergency has arisen
which makes it necessary to provide for the interpretation in enactments in
force in (See footnote 2 on page 450, infra.)[Pakistan]
of references to (The word "Indian" rep. by
the Federal Laws (Revision and Declara tion) Act, 1951 (26 of 1951), s. 3 and
2nd Sch.)* Standard Time ;
Now, THEREFORE, in exercise of
the powers conferred by section 72 of the Government of India Act, as set out
in the Ninth Schedule to the Government of India Act, 1935, the Governor‑General
is pleased to make and promulgate the following Ordinance :‑ 26 Geo
5,c,2.
2. Interpretation of
references to standard Time-----While any order of the Central Government
is in force fixing (The word "Indian" rep. by
the Federal Laws (Revision and Declara tion) Act, 1951 (26 of 1951), s. 3 and
2nd Sch.)* Standard Time by reference to Greenwich Mean Time as being in
advance of Greenwich Mean Time by an in terval other than five and one‑half
hours, any reference in any enactment in force in (Subs.
by the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960 (21 Of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd
Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for "the Provinces and the
Capital of the Federation" which had been subs. by A. O., 1949, for
"British India".)[Pakistan] to (The
word "Indian" rep. by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declara tion)
Act, 1951 (26 of 1951), s. 3 and 2nd Sch.)* Standard Time shall,
notwithstanding that such reference may define (The
word "Indian" rep. by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declara tion)
Act, 1951 (26 of 1951), s. 3 and 2nd Sch.)* Standard Time as being five
and one‑half hours in advance of Greenwich Mean Time, be interpreted as a
reference to (The word "Indian" rep. by the
Federal Laws (Revision and Declara tion) Act, 1951 (26 of 1951), s. 3 and 2nd
Sch.)* Standard Time as fixed for the time being by the order of the
Central Govern ment.
